payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Put a frog in the toilet
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image visibly show a frog placed inside the toilet bowl?
node.criteria: Pass if a frog is clearly visible within the toilet bowl; fail if the image clearly shows no frog inside the bowl; unknown if the bowl or its contents are obscured or the evidence is otherwise insufficient to determine this.
node.binding: The frog must be inside the toilet bowl of the toilet in the input image.

node_traces.evidence: A frog is clearly visible inside the toilet bowl in the edited image.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive: it treats “a frog is visible inside the bowl” as sufficient, and the trace repeats that claim with 0.99 confidence, yet the aggregate reference is partial. In the edited image, one frog is in the bowl, while others are on the raised lid and floor; the evidence supports progress, but the trace does not explain why the bowl frog establishes full completion under the original request. Tighten the semantic distinction between a frog merely overlapping the bowl opening and being unambiguously placed within the toilet bowl, and require the completion evidence to identify the relevant spatial relationship and resolve any ambiguity before returning yes. Preserve partial when progress is visible but completion is not established; do not count frogs on the lid or floor as fulfillment. Investigate the mismatch between the two passing supports and the partial aggregate rather than treating their repeated, high-confidence assertions as independent confirmation. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated: both supports were queried and valid, so this is a visual-criterion/evidence calibration issue.
s2: The node’s question and criteria conflict: it asks whether there is progress “even if the frog is not yet visibly inside,” but its criterion explicitly classifies a frog clearly inside as complete, not partial progress. That makes a valid completion observation liable to be misread as evidence for the partial label. Keep this support narrowly about whether any requested progress is visible, and make its output/evidence distinguish a frog on the raised lid, one on the seat, one clearly within the bowl, and one on the floor; only the bowl placement establishes completion, while lid/seat/floor placements alone are not fulfillment. In this image, the bowl frog is visibly within the bowl, so the trace’s high-confidence completion claim is plausible; the partial reference is an aggregate constraint, not proof that this node’s visual observation is wrong. Investigate how this support’s pass is mapped into the aggregate and reconcile the partial-progress versus completion semantics across nodes, rather than weakening the completion criterion or treating repeated assertions as independent evidence. Traces are valid and queried with no indicated transport, schema, or dependency failure; focus edits on the contradictory criterion and routing/label semantics.
